title: Security argumentation framework for SaaS buyers
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable set of talking points and objection-handling snippets for deals where security/compliance is front-and-center (healthcare, fintech, regulated marketplace platforms). This is a working field kit — lightweight, pragmatic, and intentionally modular so sellers and SEs can pick short answers or slide-ready bullets.

Audience: SDR/AE/CSE/SE/Sales engineering partners working pre-RFP & pre-SOW; also useful for product marketing to shape collateral.

TL;DR (elevator): Redwood Inference is a production-first inference platform that provides configurable deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and auditable controls that align with SOC2, ISO27001 and HIPAA needs. Our differentiators for security-conscious buyers are: 1) consistent runtime and observability across environments (reduces compliance scope), 2) strong audit telemetry and tamper-evident logs, and 3) options for customer-managed keying and private control planes.

Positioning pillars (short):
- Compliance alignment: We maintain SOC2 controls for our hosted operations and publish mappings; we provide documentation and artifacts to support customer audits.
- Deployment flexibility: Customers can move from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with the same API and telemetry, enabling progressive reduction in shared-surface risk.
- Auditability: Per-request metadata and immutable audit logs that integrate with customer SIEM/ELK solutions support forensic and compliance needs.
- Data governance controls: Configurable retention, deletion hooks, customer-managed KMS, and network isolation for private deployments.

Common buyer questions and suggested responses (concise):
1) "Can you prove you won’t see our data?"
   - Short: For Private and Dedicated we provide customer-dedicated capacity and option for customer-managed encryption keys; hosted API has strict role-based access, artifacted SOC2 controls, and telemetry showing who accessed what.
   - Evidence to offer: SOC2 report (redacted), data-flow diagram, KMS integration doc, and example audit-log extracts.

2) "What does your audit trail look like?"
   - Short: Every inference request has an immutable audit entry (request id, model version, route, timestamp, execution node id, tokens processed, and whether cached). Logs are exportable to S3/Syslog and can be streamed to customer SIEMs.
   - Technical note for SEs: Logs include hashed user identifiers (configurable) and HMACed payload digests to detect tampering. Retention configurable per customer policy.

3) "How do you handle patient/PHI data (HIPAA)?"
   - Short: We support HIPAA-ready deployments via Private or Dedicated environments, BAA available on enterprise contract, and isolated network + customer KMS options. Hosted customers can also meet many PHI use cases with strict ingestion contracts — discuss specifics with legal.

4) "How fast can we get artifacts for our auditor?"
   - Short: Standard package: SOC2 Type II summary + control mapping + sample audit logs and control narrative within 5–10 business days once contracts are signed. Private engagements: on a schedule agreed in SOW.

Audit-log language (copy-ready snippets):
- Executable snippet — short paragraph for RFPs: "Redwood Inference produces time-sequenced, tamper-evident audit logs for every inference request. Logs capture request metadata (route, model, timestamps), execution details (node, latency, cache-hit), and policy decisions (routing/fallback). Logs can be exported to the customer’s retention store or streamed to SIEMs and are HMAC-signed to detect post-hoc modifications."

- Bullet list for appendix:
  • Per-request: request_id, customer_id (configurable hash), model_version, route, start/end timestamps
  • Execution: node_id, GPU_serial (obfuscated), kernel profile, latency_ms, token_count, cache_hit
  • Policy: routing_decision, fallback_used, quota_check_result
  • Admin: operator_id, action_type, timestamp, justification

Data handling: practical commitments and options
- Ingestion control: Customers can choose to pre-process or strip PII client-side; we provide SDK hooks and server-side filters that can redact or tokenize fields before storage.
- Retention & deletion: Default hosted retention is X days (surface as a variable in sales materials); dedicated/private customers can set retention policy or request immediate deletion via API. Deletion includes kv-cache and persisted logs according to policy and is reflected in audit trail.
- Encryption: In transit TLS1.3; at-rest with AES-256. Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Isolation: Tenant-aware scheduling on Dedicated nodes; full network isolation and private control plane for Private deployments.

SOC2/ISO readiness checklist (for field use) — quick pass/fail markers to prepare evidence:
- Do we have a current SOC2 Type II? (Yes/No) -> Attach date/version
- Control mapping doc prepared for customers? -> Link in Confluence
- Sample audit logs sanitized for external review? -> Point to sample file location
- KMS integration guide available? -> Link
- BAA contract template ready? -> Legal contact name and ticket ID
- ISO27001 artifacts (scope, Statement of Applicability) available? -> If yes, provide link or timeline to certification

Competitive differentiation notes vs typical competitors (short bullets):
- Pure-managed API vendors: Redwood offers a clear path to isolation (Dedicated/Private) with identical runtime & telemetry so customers don’t need to re-architect when moving away from shared-hosting.
- Raw infra vendors: We provide audit-ready artifacts and a control plane that reduces the customer’s compliance burden vs self-hosting.
- Inference-only runtimes: Our built-in policy routing and tamper-evident logs are designed for regulated workflows (forensics, auditor requests) which many runtimes don’t surface.

Field-sell tactics and collateral recommendations:
- 1-pager: "How Redwood reduces compliance scope" (visual: single API, three deployment rails, one audit model).
- Tech checklist for SEs: two-page quick reference mapping customer controls to Redwood artifacts (where to point auditors).
- Demo: Show live audit-log stream into Splunk/Datadog, and a scripted deletion event that produces an audit entry.

Risk/ask for Product & Security teams (items to prioritize):
- Provide a templated audit-log sample set (sanitized) in the library.
- Confirm hosted-default retention numbers and make them variable placeholders for sales decks.
- Harden client SDKs with a standard pre-ingest redaction filter and add a doc showing recommended patterns for PHI tokenization.

Open questions / TODOs (internal):
- Finalize SOC2 report redaction policy with Legal (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Decide canonical text for "audit-log export" in contracts (owner: Diego).
- Create a short recording for sellers showing how to generate and parse an audit-log export (owner: Ethan).

Quick attachments to build out next:
- Slide deck: 6-slide "Security & Compliance — customer-ready" (Nora to draft).
- One-pager: evidence checklist for procurement (Maya to produce).

Notes to self (informal):
- Avoid overpromising for hosted PHI use cases; default to directing healthcare customers toward Dedicated/Private unless there’s explicit legal & architecture sign-off.
- Keep canned RFP paragraphs < 200 words to maximize pickup in procurement templates.

If you’re fielding a question and need a quick copy/paste: reach out in slack #security-sales or ping one of the collaborators above — we’ll pull the sanitized artifacts and a tailored answer.

Revision history: 2025-11-03 initial draft, 2025-12-09 added HIPAA bullets, 2026-01-18 refined audit-log fields after infra sync, 2026-02-26 added checklist items and open asks.

End.
